answer.text:

2004.14060, 2006.05880, 2010.14293, 2012.03799, 2012.08600, 2102.01444, 2106.01676, 2106.14246, 2107.12553, 2112.03161, 2201.11585, 2202.08676, 2209.07327, 2211.08028, 2302.05225, 2307.01094, 2403.01556, 2506.13565, 2508.13900, 2509.22535, 2510.07527, 2511.11853.

Strongest cases, where a single signal region is asserted (predicate region_requires_object) to require both a b-tagged jet and MET: 2006.05880 (SR-Z-1A/1B/2B), 2107.12553 (preselection), 2112.03161 (dilepton search region), 2209.07327 (ML SR), 2211.08028 (sr-gbb/sr-gtb/sr-gtt b-tagged regions). question: Which analyses use b-tagged jets (jets identified as containing a b-hadron) in their event selection?

answer.text:
46 of the 60 analyses use b-tagged jets (jets identified as containing a b-hadron) in their event selection. The concept is spread over many entity_ids because the papers spell it differently — "b-tagged jet", "$b$-tagged jet", "b-jet", "bjet", "Reconstructed/particle-level b jet", "Soft b-tag", "AK4 b-tagged jet (DeepJet/ParticleNet)", "b-tagged jet (MV2c10/DL1r/DeepCSV working point)", plus selection_requirement rows like hepkg:object_selection:bjet_count_baseline — and it is attached to selections via region_requires_object, object_has_selection, region_has_selection and result_defines_object.

Core group — signal/control regions that REQUIRE b-tagged jets (39):
2004.04545, 2004.14060, 2006.05880, 2007.02873, 2009.04363, 2010.14293, 2012.03799, 2012.08600, 2102.01444, 2103.04956, 2103.06956, 2106.01676, 2106.14246, 2107.12553, 2109.13808, 2110.11231, 2111.08340, 2112.03161, 2202.08676, 2206.09466, 2208.12095, 2209.07327, 2211.08028, 2302.05225, 2303.15340, 2307.01094, 2309.14442, 2312.04450, 2401.05299, 2402.08486, 2405.18661, 2506.13565, 2508.13900, 2509.22535, 2510.07527, 2511.11853, 2602.18611, 2604.21670, 2604.27044

question: Which analyses estimate a background using an ABCD method, or an ABCD-style sideband or matrix method over independent regions?

answer.text:
Eighteen analyses estimate a background with an ABCD method or an ABCD‑style sideband/matrix method over independent regions (all via assertion predicate background_uses_method, confirmed by the entity_facet background_methods tags "ABCD"/"Sideband" and by the quoted text).

Explicit ABCD: 2004.01678 (Modified ABCD estimate, four regions with an MC correlation correction); 2011.07812 (ABCD data‑driven background estimation method, non‑isolated→isolated muon regions); 2012.01581 (ABCD‑style ratio method using eight non‑overlapping regions A–H defined by three near‑uncorrelated criteria); 2404.06204 (two‑dimensional ABCD sideband method with control regions B, C, D for Z+multijet); 2511.11853 (ABCD/"matrix" data‑driven estimation using control regions in data with parametric fits); 2604.27044 (multidimensional ABCD reweighting, CR→SR).

Matrix method (tight/loose as the two independent regions): 2006.05880, 2106.01676, 2202.08676, 2208.12095, 2209.07327, 2307.01094.

ABCD‑style sideband / inverted‑region extrapolation: 2207.00348 (double two‑dimensional sideband method with three control regions); 2206.09466 (sideband/Z‑peak extrapolation using an inverted m_ll region scaled by the outside/inside MC fraction); 2103.06956 (nonprompt‑photon background from a photon‑ID BDT sideband control sample); 2510.07527 (background modelled from data mass sidebands); 2401.05299 (charge‑misassignment rate via a Z→ee sideband method); and, most marginally, 2008.05928, whose parametric BPDF background is validated/anchored with mass‑sideband, inverted b‑tag control samples rather than by pure ABCD counting.

question: Which analyses use the HistFitter framework for their statistical analysis?

answer.text:
Five analyses use the HistFitter statistical framework:

- 2006.05880 (ATLAS stop → tZ/tH): background from a profile-likelihood fit "implemented in the HistFitter framework," and HistFitter used for CLs 95% CL intervals.
- 2011.07812 (ATLAS displaced leptons): "The HistFitter package is used for statistical interpretation," systematic uncertainties as Gaussian nuisance parameters.
- 2106.01676 (ATLAS chargino–neutralino, 3 leptons + MET): profile log-likelihood fit on CRs and SRs implemented in HistFitter; the pyhf signal-region combination was validated against HistFitter.
- 2211.08028 (ATLAS MET + ≥3 b-jets): per-SR background-only profile-likelihood fits implemented in HistFitter.
- 2102.01444 (ATLAS two opposite-charge leptons + jets + MET): simultaneous likelihood fits performed "using standard minimisation software packages, HistFitter and pyhf" (attested in the paper text; no HistFitter entity/assertion was extracted for this paper).

The relevant graph entities are hepkg:method:histfitter, hepkg:method:profile-likelihood-fit, hepkg:method:profile-likelihood-fit-histfitter and hepkg:method:pyhf-combination, linked via result_uses_statistical_method. HistFitter appears only as a reference-list citation (not as an analysis tool) in 2004.14060, 2009.14537, 2010.14293 and 2307.01094, so those are excluded.

question: Which analyses unfold their measured distributions -- that is, correct them back to particle level or truth level?

answer.text:
Sixteen analyses unfold their measured distributions back to particle/truth/generator/parton level:

- 2001.06899 — TUnfold least-squares unfolding of differential Z+b/c distributions (particle-level leptons and jets)
- 2103.04956 — unfolding of detector effects from observed H→4ℓ distributions via response matrices; particle-level fiducial phase space
- 2110.11231 — TUnfold least-squares regularized unfolding with area constraint → unfolded WZ differential cross sections
- 2112.00895 — "cross sections are unfolded to the parton level" (W+c at 8 TeV)
- 2206.09466 — "results are then unfolded to the generator level" per STXS bin (H→WW*)
- 2207.12246 — iterative dynamically-stabilized unfolding plus SVD unfolding cross-check, migration matrices and data-driven closure test (elastic pp scattering)
- 2208.12095 — Fully Bayesian Unfolding (FBU) for the tt̄ charge asymmetry
- 2303.15340 — bin-by-bin unfolding with explicit particle→detector bin-migration handling (dilepton tt̄)
- 2308.02285 — unfolding of measurements to particle and parton levels (W+c at 13 TeV)
- 2309.14442 — binned maximum-likelihood fit for unfolding, tt̄bb̄ differential measurements with particle-level objects
- 2312.04450 — profile-likelihood unfolding (PLU) with Tikhonov regularisation → particle-level differential tt̄V cross sections
- 2401.05299 — profile-likelihood unfolding with Tikhonov regularisation, Asimov closure/bias stress tests
- 2402.08486 — TUnfold χ²-fit unfolding with Tikhonov regularization plus pseudo-data closure/coverage test
- 2404.06204 — iterative Bayesian (D'Agostini) unfolding of W± and Z p_T spectra at 5.02 and 13 TeV
- 2506.13565 — TUnfold correction of bin-by-bin mass-scale/resolution migration in high-mass dilepton spectra
- 2504.13081 — combination reporting unfolded differential Higgs cross sections, fitted with one parameter of interest per generator-level bin

Deliberately excluded: 2405.18661 and 2604.21670, which only quote/interpret other experiments' already-unfolded results rather than performing an unfolding, and 2408.03744, whose "binned maximum likelihood fit for unfolding" is only a rollup entity label — the paper's own label is a fit to m_T and m_ll distributions for inclusive cross sections, with no unfolding in the text.

question: Which analyses reconstruct a Higgs-boson candidate as a physical object they select on (rather than merely studying Higgs production or decay)?

answer.text:
Thirteen analyses reconstruct a Higgs-boson candidate as a real object they define and cut on (via result_defines_object / region_requires_object / object_has_selection on a detector_object that is the Higgs candidate itself):

- 2004.04545 — hepkg:object:diphoton_system ("Diphoton system (H→γγ candidate)") in ttH/tH
- 2006.05880 — hepkg:object:higgs-boson-candidate ("Higgs boson candidate, h→bb jet pair, NN-tagged"), required in SR^h_1A/1B/1AB
- 2008.05928 — hepkg:object:largeR-jet ("Large-R jet, H→bb̄ candidate J"), required in the single/double-b-tag SRs and the sideband CR
- 2103.04956 — hepkg:object:zz_candidate ("ZZ candidate, four-lepton Higgs boson candidate")
- 2103.06956 — hepkg:object:diphoton_system (H→γγ candidate)
- 2107.12553 — hepkg:object:h-tagged-jet ("H-tagged large-R jet, H→bb"), required in all 12 signal regions
- 2111.08340 — hepkg:object:H-jet / hepkg:object:candidate-jet / hepkg:object:double-tagged-candidate-jet, required in SRL/SRS (anti-tagged variant vetoed in VRL/VRS)
- 2112.03161 — hepkg:object:bb_jet ("H→bb candidate jet"), required in the SL/DL signal regions and non-top CR
- 2207.00348 — hepkg:object:diphoton-system (and hepkg:object:higgs-boson-particle-level), with explicit object_has_selection: two-leading-photon definition, diphoton mass window, Higgs rapidity fiducial
- 2504.13081 — hepkg:object:higgs_boson ("Higgs boson (reconstructed candidate)")
- 2602.18611 — hepkg:object:large_radius_jet ("Large-radius jet, boosted H→bb"), required in hbb_boosted_ggh/hbb_boosted_vbf
- 2604.27044 — hepkg:object:h-candidate-merged and hepkg:object:h-candidate-resolved (HH→4b), required in the merged/resolved signal regions
- 2605.14245 — hepkg:object:diphoton ("Diphoton system (Higgs boson candidate)"), required in the diphoton preselection region

Excluded because they only study Higgs production/decay without a Higgs-candidate object in the selection: 2007.02873 (VH H→bb, only b-tagged AK4 jets), 2009.04363 (H→μμ), 2109.13808 (H→WW*jj), 2201.11585 (invisible Higgs, VBF jets + MET), 2205.05120, 2206.09466, 2004.01678 (H→Z + light resonance), and 2012.08600 (its large-R jet is labelled a W/Z boson candidate, not a Higgs candidate).

question: Which analyses have a ttZ background and a control region used to normalise that background?

answer.text:
Seven analyses in the graph have a ttZ background that is normalised in a dedicated control region:

• 2006.05880 (ATLAS stop, H/Z+jets) — ttZ background (hepkg:background:ttZ-3l) normalised via CR^Z_ttZ (hepkg:object:CR-Z-ttZ), profile-likelihood fit extrapolated to the SR.
• 2102.01444 (CMS squark/DM 2-,3-,4-body) — tt̄+Z background normalised to data in CR_{tt̄Z}.
• 2110.11231 (CMS WZ cross-section/TGC) — ttZ+tZq irreducible background constrained by CR-ttZ (hepkg:region:cr-ttz) with a free-floating normalisation in the combined fit.
• 2202.08676 (CMS inclusive multilepton) — ttZ irreducible background normalised to data in the 3L ttZ control region (hepkg:region:3l-ttz-cr).
• 2401.05299 (ATLAS tt̄W) — tt̄Z/γ* normalised in the 3ℓ ttZ CR (fitted λ_tt̄Z = 1.16 ± 0.15).
• 2004.14060 (ATLAS all-hadronic tt̄+MET) — tt̄+Z background estimated in CRTTZ (hepkg:region:crttz), with a dedicated "$t\bar t+Z$ background estimation" section.
• 2012.08600 (CMS SUSY, 2 SF leptons + MET) — the Z+X category containing ttZ is simulated then normalised/validated in dedicated trilepton and 4-lepton control regions.

Borderline: 2106.14246 defines a ttZ-enriched control region but records its ttX (tttt/ttH/ttW/ttZ) background as a direct simulation estimate, so no CR normalisation of ttZ is asserted. Excluded: 2405.18661 (ttZ is the signal measurement, not a background), 2309.14442 (ttX normalised to NNLO/NLO theory), 2009.04363 and 2103.04956 (MC/parametric-fit estimates, no ttZ CR).

question: Which analyses require exactly two electrons OR exactly two muons as alternative selections -- parallel ee and mumu channels, rather than requiring both?

answer.text:
Analyses that define an "exactly two electrons" and an "exactly two muons" selection as ALTERNATIVE, parallel dilepton categories (ee or μμ, not both at once):

- 2503.19420 — sibling regions "Same-sign 2-electron signal region" (hepkg:region:ss2e-sr) and "Same-sign 2-muon signal region" (hepkg:region:ss2mu-sr).
- 2511.11853 — "Dimuon (mu+mu-) channel" with SR_b/SR_{b+j/b}/CR_j/CR_2j mirrored by the "Dielectron (e+e-) control channel" with CR_b^{ee}/CR_{b+j/b}^{ee}/CR_j^{ee}/CR_2j^{ee}.
- 2506.13565 — channels written explicitly as "ℓ+ℓ− (ee or μμ) + 0 / exactly 1 / ≥2 b-tagged jets", plus the R(mumu/ee) ratio observable.
- 2208.12095 — regions "Dilepton $ee+\mu\mu$, 1$b$-tag-exclusive" and "Dilepton $ee+\mu\mu$, 2$b$-tag-inclusive" (the two flavours summed as alternatives).
- 2509.22535 — separate "2L channel electron selection" (hepkg:object_selection:electron_2L) and "2L channel muon selection" (hepkg:object_selection:muon_2L) under the shared two-opposite-charge-lepton requirement.
- 2009.14537 — "ee+p (electron pair plus tagged forward proton)" and "μμ+p (muon pair plus tagged forward proton)" as two independent channels, with systematics quoted per channel ("ee: 2%, mumu: 3%").
- 2102.01444 — channel "Two opposite-charge leptons (electrons or muons), jets and missing transverse momentum".

By contrast, 2009.04363 and 2602.18611 are muon-pair only, and 2011.07812 (ee, μμ, or emu) and 2103.04956 (4e, 4μ, 2e2μ) mix flavours rather than giving a clean ee-or-μμ pair.

question: Which analyses reconstruct a Higgs-boson candidate as a physical object they select on (rather than merely studying Higgs production or decay)?

answer.text:
Analyses that reconstruct a Higgs-boson candidate as an actual selected object (the Higgs appears as a detector_object/object_definition carrying object_has_selection assertions, rather than only as a physics_process or observable):

- 2004.04545 — hepkg:object:diphoton_system "Diphoton system (H→γγ candidate)", cut on m_γγ ∈ [105,160] GeV
- 2006.05880 — hepkg:object:higgs-boson-candidate "Higgs boson candidate (h→bb jet pair, NN-tagged)"
- 2008.05928 — hepkg:object:largeR-jet "Large-R jet (H→bb̄ candidate, J)", mass window around m_H = 125.80 GeV parameterised in jet pT
- 2012.08600 — hepkg:object:large_radius_jet "(boosted H→bb analysis)": pT>200 GeV, soft-drop mass 65–105 GeV, τ21 2-prong requirement
- 2103.04956 — hepkg:object:zz_candidate "four-lepton Higgs boson candidate", 105 < m(4ℓ) < 140 GeV
- 2103.06956 — hepkg:object:diphoton_system "Diphoton system (H→γγ candidate)" with diphoton mass selection
- 2107.12553 — hepkg:object:h-tagged-jet "H-tagged large-R jet (H to bb)", DeepAK8 mass-decorrelated H-tagger working point
- 2111.08340 — hepkg:object:candidate-jet / hepkg:object:H-jet: leading-or-subleading jet, |η|<2, pT>250 GeV, m_J>60 GeV, 2m_J/pT<1, ≥2 track-jets
- 2112.03161 — hepkg:object:bb_jet "H→bb candidate jet": pT>200 GeV, two soft-drop subjets, Z/H→bb tagger loose/tight categories
- 2207.00348 — hepkg:object:diphoton-system: two leading photons forming the diphoton system, 105–160 GeV mass window
- 2504.13081 — hepkg:object:higgs_boson "Higgs boson (reconstructed candidate)", transverse mass > 60 GeV
- 2604.27044 — hepkg:object:h-candidate-resolved and hepkg:object:h-candidate-merged (bb dijet from two AK4 b-jets, or single AK8 jet)
- 2605.14245 — hepkg:object:diphoton "Diphoton system (Higgs boson candidate)" with mass selection

Deliberately excluded: papers that only study Higgs production/decay or select the Higgs decay products without forming a candidate object (e.g. 2007.02873, 2009.04363, 2109.13808, 2604.21670, 2206.09466, 2205.05120, 2302.05225), the combination paper 2602.18611 (it mentions a boosted H→bb large-radius jet but records no selection on it), and papers whose dilepton/Z candidates are used to veto or reconstruct vector bosons rather than a Higgs (2009.14537, 2001.06899, 2408.03744).

question: Which analyses require exactly two electrons OR exactly two muons as alternative selections -- parallel ee and mumu channels, rather than requiring both?

answer.text:
Analyses that impose an "exactly two electrons" OR "exactly two muons" choice — i.e. parallel ee and μμ channels, not a requirement of both — are:

• 2009.14537 — two alternative final states ee+p (hepkg:final_state:ee-plus-p) and μμ+p (hepkg:final_state:mumu-plus-p), with per-channel systematics (e.g. hepkg:systematic:pileup-modeling-ccent, "ee: 2%, mumu: 3%").
• 2011.07812 — displaced dilepton defined as "Two displaced leptons (ee, mumu, or emu)" (hepkg:final_state:displaced-dilepton) with independent regions hepkg:region:sr-ee and hepkg:region:sr-mumu (plus VR-ee/VR-eμ variants).
• 2112.03161 — lepton-flavour categorisation "Two electrons or two muons → SF" (vs one e + one μ → OF).
• 2206.09466 — same-flavour ggH categories targeting "either two electrons or two muons".
• 2208.12095 — hepkg:region:dl_eeMumu_2b_incl, the "Dilepton ee + μμ" region, kept as the OR of the two same-flavour modes and separate from hepkg:region:dl_emu_2b_incl.
• 2503.19420 — separate hepkg:region:ss2e-sr (same-sign 2-electron) and hepkg:region:ss2mu-sr (same-sign 2-muon) signal regions.
• 2509.22535 — the 2L channel carries two alternative object selections, hepkg:object_selection:electron_2L and hepkg:object_selection:muon_2L, under the shared hepkg:object_selection:lepton_req_2L ("two opposite-charge leptons") requirement.

Partial/borderline: 2511.11853 has both hepkg:channel:dimuon and hepkg:channel:dielectron, but the ee mode is a control channel to the μμ signal rather than an equivalent alternative selection; 2004.14060 and 2012.03799 use "two electrons or muons (ℓ) from Z decays" only inside Z(ℓℓ)+jets control regions; 2009.04363 (H→μμ) is muon-only in its signal categories.

Papers: 2009.14537, 2011.07812, 2503.19420, 2506.13565
